title.rendered: The Battle Is Not Yours: Jehoshaphat and the Rest of Surrender | Living from Rest, Day 12

excerpt.rendered: Three armies were marching on Judah. God told the king to stand still and watch. Day 12 of Living from Rest unpacks the rest of surrender in battle.

content.rendered:
Jehoshaphat’s army did not swing a sword. They sang. The battle was fought for them while they worshipped. There is a rest even in warfare.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, November 12, 2026 | Living from Rest, Day 12

Today’s Scripture

“And he said, ‘Listen, all you of Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat! Thus says the Lord to you: Do not be afraid nor dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God’s.’”
2 Chronicles 20:15 (NKJV)

“You will not need to fight in this battle. Position yourselves, stand still and see the salvation of the Lord, who is with you, O Judah and Jerusalem!”
2 Chronicles 20:17 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Second Chronicles 20 is one of the most dramatic rest stories in the Bible. Three enemy armies, Moab, Ammon, and Mount Seir, had united to invade Judah. Jehoshaphat, the king, received the news and did the most strategic thing he could have done: he feared, and he set himself to seek the Lord. He proclaimed a national fast. He gathered the people in the courtyard of the temple. He prayed one of the most honest prayers in Scripture: “We have no power against this great multitude that is coming against us; nor do we know what to do, but our eyes are upon You.”

Then God answered through the prophet Jahaziel. Second Chronicles 20:15, in the NKJV, says, “Do not be afraid nor dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” The AMPC says, “Be not afraid or dismayed at this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.” The TPT says, “Do not be afraid, and do not be discouraged by this huge army, for the battle is not yours but God’s.”

The next verse upgrades the rest. “You will not need to fight in this battle. Position yourselves, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord.” Position. Stand still. See. That is the posture of a soldier at rest. Judah still has to show up. They still have to march out. But the weapon in their hand is not a sword. The weapon is a song. Jehoshaphat appoints singers to walk in front of the army, giving praise “to the beauty of holiness.” As they begin to sing, the Lord sets ambushes against the enemy, and the three armies turn on each other. Judah does not swing a sword all day. They collect the spoils for three days.

You may be walking into a day that feels like three armies have joined forces against you. Debt and sickness and a difficult relationship. Grief, pressure, and a job that is on the line. Hear the word God sent Jahaziel to Jehoshaphat. The battle is not yours. Position yourself. Stand still. See the salvation of the Lord. Replace the sword in your hand with a song in your mouth. The One who fought for Judah will fight for you.

The Four Movements of Resting Warfare

Fear and seek. Admit the fear, and set your face to seek the Lord.

Pray honestly. “We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on You.”

Position and worship. Stand still. Lift the song. Walk out singing.

Collect the spoils. Watch God fight battles you could never have won.

Declaration

Lord, I thank You that the battle is not mine; it is Yours (2 Chronicles 20:15). Thank You that in Christ the victory is already won; You have given me the victory through my Lord Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 15:57). I am not afraid of the armies gathered against me. My eyes are on You. I position myself, I stand still, and I lift a song of praise. You fight for me, and I see Your salvation. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
